01 · The idea

A curiosity engine turns what you read into a graph you can reason over.

Curiosity Engine (CE) ingests raw sources — papers, notes, tables — and distills them into a typed, interlinked wiki. Not a folder of documents: a knowledge graph, where a retrieval agent can follow structure, not just match keywords.

04 · The ontology

A meta-ontology gives an agent typed handholds.

Every page is one of twelve types with a defined role, so an agent knows what it's reading and how pieces connect — the structure that makes graph reasoning tractable.

Edge types
WikiLink · Cites · DataRef · Depicts · AppearsIn
Identity layer
Generalized IRI (Internationalized Resource Identifier) registry ce:<class>:<workspace>:<slug> — any entity class, minted locally. same_as merges duplicates; curiosity-merge reconciles entities across workspaces. Extract, then merge.

05 · Trust

The graph stays honest: propose → review, never blind writes.

An agent never edits the wiki directly. Every change is staged, then vetted by a stronger reviewer model — so a cheap model can safely do the legwork while the graph stays clean.

agent

Proposes

propose_wiki_page / propose_page_edit stage a draft — the agent has no way to write the wiki directly.

→
reviewer model

Vets it

A stronger model scores the draft — accuracy weighted hardest, the gate against a small model's confident hallucinations.

→
verdict

Accept · edit · reject

Clean pages file themselves; the rest are caught before they touch the graph.

Accept

A clean page files itself into the wiki and schedules a background graph rebuild.

Borderline

Becomes an accept/reject card in the rail; View opens the draft plus the reviewer's annotations.

Reject

Dropped with the reason. And there is no delete-page tool — writes stage, they never destroy.

Reads are provably safe. Grounding a question — search_wiki, read_wiki_page, wiki_neighbors — is read-only, so it never interrupts you with a permission card. Only writes pass through the gate.

06 · Does it work?

Curation + graph beat raw-vault RAG on facts & multi-hop — on two frontier models.

curiosity-test · 150 Qs Fable-5 + gpt-5.6 · frontier · low effort answers from each arm's context only cross-judged — each model judges both sets n=50/cat

keyword		 A1
graph		 B
RAG·vault		 B′
RAG·wiki		 R
routed

Bars: blue = correctness (per generator) · orange = retrieval recall (a retrieval property — same for both generators) · green = global win-rate vs B, length-controlled (0.5 = tie; a soft, judge-noisy edge — see H3 + Appendix G). A0 keyword · A1 graph · B raw-vault RAG baseline · B′ RAG-wiki · R routed (shipped). Older sonnet-4.6 numbers: Appendix D. n=50/cat.

Hypotheses & outcomes — each tag's colour = the metric it tests, matching the bars
H1
Single-hop facts — curation + graph beat raw-vault RAG. Confirmed. On single-hop correctness, B′/R ≈0.93 (Fable-5), 0.81 (gpt-5.6) vs raw-vault RAG (B) 0.64/0.53; keyword (A0) the weakest arm. A clear win on both frontier models, not parity.
H2
Multi-hop synthesis — the same advantage holds. Confirmed. B′ led multi-hop correctness (0.68 Fable, 0.54 gpt-5.6); raw-vault RAG was lowest (0.47/0.39) — it found the sources but didn't synthesise. Same ordering on both models.
H3
Open-ended sensemaking — does curation help? Mostly answer length, not curation. The global "win" flipped by generator because the metric tracked verbosity; length-controlled (Appendix G) both models only modestly favour curation (0.58–0.79) — a soft, judge-noisy edge.
H4
Retrieval recall — did the arms find the right sources? Raw-vault RAG's recall is high (0.84 single, 0.76 multi) — it finds the sources but (H2) doesn't synthesise them. Routing (R) keeps recall high (0.88 / 0.77) while topping correctness; keyword (A0) lowest throughout (0.30).
Net
Curated-wiki (B′) + light routing (R) are the top arms. Top-tier on every correctness metric across both frontier generators — curation plus per-type routing, no exotic machinery.

07 · Where we are

Curation is the win; the graph adds the connective edge.

01
Curation is most of the value. Plain vector RAG over the curated wiki (the RAG-wiki arm) was strong everywhere — the distilled, linked pages carry the weight, retrievable by simple embeddings.
02
Curated + graph beat raw-vault RAG — robustly. On two frontier models (Fable-5, gpt-5.6, cross-judged) the RAG-wiki and routed arms topped both factoid and multi-hop correctness; raw-vault RAG and keyword lagged. The ordering didn't move with the model.
03
Fancier isn't always better. Swapping breadth-first-search traversal for Personalized PageRank didn't help at this corpus scale — it was significantly worse on global. Personalized PageRank is a play for much larger graphs.
04
The winning retrieval policy is simple routing. Send each question type to its best retriever — curated-wiki for factoids, hybrid for multi-hop. Best of both, no exotic machinery.
Breadth-first-search traversal
Walks the graph outward hop by hop from the seed pages, ranking neighbours by graph distance — local and cheap. The traversal that won here.
Personalized PageRank
A random-walk score seeded on the query's pages that ranks the whole graph by proximity in one shot (HippoRAG's method) — built for much larger graphs.
So, then —

What do you actually do with a graph like this?

That's where Switch Bay comes in.

Appendix A · running CE from Switch Bay economically

Where to spend tokens — and where not to.

Everything above tested which retrieval wins. This is the operational read: given those results, the cheapest configuration that keeps the quality ordering intact.

The recommended ladder
$0 local
Retrieve on-device
CE's shipped retrieval — embeddings, FTS5, graph traversal — runs locally. The whole retrieval layer costs no tokens; the arm that wins (vector-seeded BFS + routing) is free to run.
low $
Answer with a mid-tier model at low effort
Quality saturates early: the correctness ordering held from sonnet-4.6 / gpt-4.1 → Fable-5 / gpt-5.6, and a high-effort A/B added no signal. Pay for reasoning effort only if a task actually needs it.
premium
Reserve the strong model for the curate gate
Spend the frontier model where it changes outcomes — the propose→review step that writes the wiki — not on every per-query answer. Curation is amortized across every future retrieval.
Why this is safe to do
  • Ordering is model-robust — curated arms beat raw-vault RAG on facts & multi-hop across two model generations, so a cheaper current model preserves the win.
  • Effort saturates — low vs high effort didn't move the ranking; the scores already max out on these tasks.
  • Retrieval is the free lever — the biggest quality gain (curation + graph) is a one-time build cost, then $0 per query.
Can a local model do the paid work? — partly
Earlier testing with a local 9B (Ornith 9B) found it insufficient for the hard, agentic path: it reasoned adaptively but couldn't complete a curation run (hit turn caps, missing a tool), and ran ~4× slower. It is viable as a cheap bulk worker — fan-out extraction / triage that moves ~65% of tokens off the paid model. So the net config is a model ladder: trivial & high-volume → local; hard & agentic → strong.

Appendix B · glossary (1 / 2)

Terms & algorithms — data, knowledge & retrieval.

Stores & indexes
Vault — the store of raw sources, verbatim; the recall layer. Backed by vault.db.
Wiki — the distilled, typed, interlinked markdown pages; the curated knowledge the graph is built over.
vault.db — a SQLite database holding each source's extracted text plus its two search indexes (FTS5 + embeddings).
FTS5 — SQLite's built-in full-text search (BM25-style keyword ranking). Indexes the whole source text — the lossless lexical layer.
sqlite-vec — a SQLite extension for vector (nearest-neighbour) search; stores the source_embeddings index.
source_embeddings — one dense vector per whole source (MiniLM, 384-dim, first ~8k chars). No chunking; enables semantic search.
Kuzu (graph.kuzu) — an embedded property-graph database; holds the typed node/edge graph (WikiPage / VaultSource nodes) queried for structure.
conversations.db — machine-local SQLite (WAL) storing rail threads / runs / turns; kept off cloud-sync by default.
Ontology & identity
Typed pages (9 kinds) — concept · entity · fact · evidence · analysis · figure · table · source · note. Every wiki page is one, giving an agent typed handholds.
Edge types — WikiLink (page→page), Cites (page→source), DataRef, Depicts, AppearsIn — the typed relations in the graph.
Curator — CE's curation skill loop: extract typed pages from sources, then link, promote & dedupe them into the graph.
Propose → review — writes are never blind: an agent stages a draft (propose_wiki_page / propose_page_edit); a stronger reviewer model rules accept / edit / reject. No delete-page tool.
IRI — Internationalized Resource Identifier; CE's generalized identity key ce:<class>:<workspace>:<slug>, minted locally for any entity class.
same_as — an identity relation that merges duplicate entities into one.
curiosity-merge — reconciles entities across different workspaces.
Retrieval & graph algorithms
Embedding / cosine similarity — text → a dense vector; relatedness is the cosine (dot product of unit vectors). The basis of semantic search.
RAG — Retrieval-Augmented Generation: retrieve passages, stuff them into the prompt, generate. The baseline family (arms B / B′).
Hybrid retrieval + RRF — blend FTS keyword and vector rankings via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (a rank-based score fusion). CE's vault_search --mode hybrid.
BFS traversal — breadth-first graph expansion outward from seed pages, ranking neighbours by hop distance. Local, cheap — the traversal that led this benchmark.
Personalized PageRank (PPR) — a random-walk proximity score seeded on the query's pages, ranking the whole graph in one shot (HippoRAG's method). A play for very large graphs (rejected at this scale).
Vector-seeded graph traversal (GraphRAG) — a semantic seed page, then graph expansion; isolates the graph's contribution (arm A1).
Adaptive routing (arm R) — send each query type to its best retriever: single-hop → RAG-wiki, multi-hop → hybrid, global → graph-only. The shipped policy.
Benchmark arms — A0 keyword · A1 graph (BFS) · A1P graph (PPR) · B RAG-vault · B′ RAG-wiki · H fixed hybrid · HA adaptive-over-PPR · R adaptive-over-BFS.

Appendix B · glossary (2 / 2)

Terms & architecture — system, protocols & evaluation.

Runtime & architecture
Daemon — the always-on local process (Python, aiohttp) that owns everything: LLM providers, the tool registry, rail history, PTY sessions, the local model server. Runs as a launchd agent — closing the window doesn't stop work.
Web app / frontend — a React Progressive Web App served from 127.0.0.1:8765; the surface only, with no logic or state authority.
PWA — Progressive Web App: installable, runs in its own window, works offline.
WebSocket + REST — the two daemon channels: WS streams live agent events; REST (/api/*) for requests. Both Origin/Host-guarded.
PTY — pseudo-terminal; real bash / CLI sessions in the rail (the !cmd shell path).
llmgateway — the provider abstraction: hosted APIs (Anthropic · xAI · OpenAI · Gemini), coding CLIs (Claude Code · Grok Build · Codex), or local llama.cpp / Ollama — your keys, one interface.
Model ladder — mixing providers by difficulty within one fan-out (cheap rungs for easy steps, strong for hard).
Fan-out — one run becomes many: a planner decomposes, N subprocess workers run in parallel (isolated, killable), a merger synthesizes.
Rail — the agent-conversation column (chat, tool cards, reasoning, permission cards); detects shell commands and keeps threads.
Power / Zen mode — the two cockpits: Power = 3-column browser / tabs / rail; Zen = think at the graph (graph left, one surface right, floating chat).
Report artifact — create_report renders model-authored HTML in a sandboxed iframe (Report tab); the chat reply shrinks to a one-line link.
Workspace → Thread → Run → Turn — the scope hierarchy: a knowledge base → a durable conversation → one dispatch → one user↔assistant exchange.
Atomic writes — temp-file + fsync + os.replace so a crash mid-write can't corrupt state.
Interop protocols
A2A (Agent-to-Agent) — an Agent Card + JSON-RPC (message/send, tasks/get); thread ↔ contextId, run ↔ Task id. Powers cross-thread / cross-workspace agent calls (ask_thread).
AG-UI — the agent-run event protocol: lifecycle events (RUN_STARTED, TOOL_CALL_*, …) over WebSocket; Switch Bay specifics ride as CUSTOM events. Works with any AG-UI client (e.g. CopilotKit).
MCP (Model Context Protocol) — the tool / skill bridge: capabilities exposed as MCP tools (load_skill, get_skill, workspace tools) so subprocess models reach the same tool surface.
Models & embeddings
MiniLM (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) — CE's default embedding model; 384-dim, ~512-token (~2k-char) context. Fast, local, CPU-friendly.
fastembed — the light ONNX embedding runtime Switch Bay uses (default bge-small-en-v1.5, 384-dim, no PyTorch) for the curated-wiki vector index (arm B′).
nomic-embed — a longer-context (8k-token) embedding alternative the 8k-char cap leaves room for.
Evaluation methodology
LLM-as-judge — a model scores answer correctness, or picks the better of two answers — the grading mechanism.
Position bias — a judge favouring the first (or second) option regardless of content; controlled by scoring both orderings.
Bootstrap CI — confidence intervals by resampling; how significance is reported (paired for arm-vs-arm deltas).
Inter-judge agreement — the score spread across the 4-judge panel (σ 0.047 here); tight = panel-robust, not one judge's artifact.

Appendix C · what the task types test

The three question types — real examples from the benchmark.

Drawn verbatim from the 150-question curiosity-test set (an ML-research corpus). Difficulty escalates from one-fact lookup to whole-corpus synthesis.

single-hopone fact on one page — retrieve the passage, read the value
QWhat patch size does Dosovitskiy et al. (2020) use when splitting images for the Vision Transformer? → 16×16 pixels
QWhat reward signals trained DeepSeek-R1 via pure RL, with no supervised chain-of-thought data? → verifiable rewards in math, coding & STEM
multi-hopchain two or more facts across pages — the graph's home ground
QGPT is autoregressive and built on a specific architecture — what core mechanism does that architecture use instead of recurrence or convolutions, and in what year was it introduced? → Transformer self-attention, 2017
QDeepSeek-V2 is cited as a mainstream Mixture-of-Experts model — how many total parameters does it have, and what fraction are activated per token? → 236B total, ≈21B (~9%) active
global · sensemakingsynthesize a theme across the whole corpus — no single passage answers it
QAcross the corpus, how do State Space Models like Mamba compare to Transformers and hybrid architectures on the trade-offs between efficiency, long-context modelling, and reasoning quality — a genuine replacement for attention, or a complementary component?
QHow do routing strategies, load-balancing, and expert-granularity choices in MoE architectures (Switch, Mixtral, DeepSeek-V2) trade off training stability, inference efficiency, and model quality?

Appendix E · why PPR lost

Personalized PageRank did not beat BFS at this scale.

Comparison (A1P − A1)Δ95% CIVerdict
single-hop correctness−0.022[−.059,+.004]tie
single-hop recall−0.040[−.120,+.040]tie
multi-hop correctness+0.010[−.075,+.098]tie
multi-hop recall−0.060[−.160,+.040]tie

01
Only the global result clears zero — and it clears it the wrong way. Everything else is a statistical tie.
02
PPR's teleport concentrates mass on hub pages. That costs diversity — exactly what the global / sensemaking metric rewards.
03
It's a scale play. At 384 pages, BFS distance-ranking wins. Revisit PPR only if the graph grows orders of magnitude larger.
04
Routing over BFS is the fix (arm R). Sending each query type to its winning retriever recovers the top global (0.90 vs the PPR-routed 0.81) while keeping the best factoid and multi-hop — measured, not projected.

Appendix G · follow-up experiment

Is sensemaking a real win, or just answer length?

H3 exposed the global "comprehensiveness" result as length-confounded — it flipped by generator because the metric tracks how long the answer is. This follow-up removes the confound.

Setup
  • the 50 global / sensemaking questions
  • every arm's answer capped to ≤ 80 words — the same budget, so length can't win it
  • Fable-5 + gpt-5.6 generate; cross-judged on comprehensiveness & diversity, both orderings
How to read it
Win-rate vs raw-vault RAG (B); 0.5 = tie. Curated arms still beating B with length equalized ⇒ sensemaking is a real retrieval effect. Collapse to ~0.5 ⇒ it was verbosity all along.
Result — global win-rate vs raw-vault RAG (0.5 = tie)
A0A1B′Runcontrolled
Fable-50.680.780.750.790.79–0.92
gpt-5.60.590.590.580.590.41–0.49 ↺
The reversal was verbosity. Length-matched, gpt-5.6's curated arms went from losing to raw-vault RAG (0.41–0.49) to slightly winning (0.58–0.59). So both models now favour curation on sensemaking — but modestly, not the old 0.91. And the two judges disagreed heavily (|Δ|=0.53) on short-answer comprehensiveness → a soft, noisy edge. Factoid + multi-hop stay the strong, robust wins.

Appendix H · synonym / alias resolution (H5)

Curation resolves aliases that raw-vault RAG can't.

Pre-registered, end-to-end: 24 invented entities hidden in the real 392-page corpus, each queried by its canonical name (a positive control) and by an alias. A cheap model answers from each arm's retrieved context; scoring is exact gold-value match — no judge.

Two alias families (length-balanced)
  • real synonym — a name the model/embeddings know (heart attack ≈ myocardial infarction)
  • invented codename — a coined alias, linked only by a definition doc (Project Zephyr = "the customer-churn prediction service")
  • control — look-alike names with no entity (Marlon vs Marlin) → should abstain
Why it's a fair test
Needles sit in a real haystack (retrieval must discriminate, not scan 20%). Every arm gets the same budget + same generator, so raw RAG can retrieve the definition and the fact and reason over both — the metric doesn't handicap it. The canonical-name query is a built-in positive control.
Answer accuracy — cheap model, from each arm's retrieved context

Queried by the canonical name, everyone answers perfectly (control passes). Switch to an alias and raw-vault RAG collapses — 0.67 on real synonyms (embedding proximity half-saves it), 0.00 on invented codenames: it retrieves the definition but the fact stays an unreachable needle. Curated wiki-RAG holds at 1.00. B's alias penalty: 0.33 (synonym) → 1.00 (codename), exactly as pre-registered.
n=24 entities in a 392-page haystack, one curation run, gemini-2.5-flash. Pre-registered; the refutation condition didn't trigger. Keyword search (A0, omitted) failed even the control — poor for natural-language queries.

Appendix I · semantic dissonance (H6)

Same name, different things — curation keeps them apart.

The dual of H5. H5: different names, one entity → curation must merge. H6: the same name means different things in two projects → curation must split. The risk it tests: does curation over-merge a homonym into one incoherent page?

Setup
A coined term (e.g. the Doohickey) is used in two projects with a distinct sense + figure — a process ("Atlas: validation step, 3,412 records") vs an output ("Borealis: ledger file, 88.4 MB") — hidden in the 392-page haystack.
Curation passed the structural test
It wrote two provenanced pages per term (Doohickey · Atlas / Doohickey · Borealis) — it did not over-merge them. When the query names the project (H6a), every arm answers the right sense — no gap.

Given an ambiguous term, raw-vault RAG collapses to a single sense (0.20) — it silently answers one meaning and drops the other, so the user never learns there were two. Curated retrieval surfaces both and attributes each to its project (B′ 1.00, routed 0.90). The provenanced split is what makes the ambiguity visible.
